newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude off sharply after breaking key support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude off sharply after breaking key support.

text.p: NYMEX crude was off sharply Monday afternoon after the spot month broke key technical support of $26.00, steepening declines in heating oil which was already weakened by forecasts of warmer temperatures in the U.S. East Coast.

"It started with some regional forecasters calling for warmer temperatures, and then heat just rode down with crude after it (crude) failed to hold $26.00," said Al Lindseth, manager of oil and gas hedge programs at GSC Energy.
At 1314 EST, February crude was off 45 cents at $25.64 a barrel after falling to a session low of $25.50.
February heating oil was off 1.75 cents at 70.40 cents a gallon while February gasoline was off 2.01 cents at 68.35 cents gallon.
"It's mainly technical now," said Bob Yawger, trader with E.D. & F. Man International, of crude's sell-off.

"There were some sell stops at $26.00 and $25.90. You can bet there will be some sell stops below $25.21," Yawger said, citing 38 percent retracement of the move from Feb crude's low December 11 of $22.73 to its contract high of $26.74 January 9.

In the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States, temperatures are forecasted to warm to normal Tuesday through Thursday before a cold snap is expected to send temperatures eight to 10 degrees below normal during the weekend, said Charlie Notis, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather in Des Moines, Iowa.
But, temperatures are seen rising from lower levels again next week when they will fluctuate between normal and slightly below normal levels, Notis said.

By late next week, a cold airmass will move across the Midwest into the Northeast, but the cold front will be weaker than the one experienced by the Northeast this past weekend, said meteorologist Jon Davis of Smith Barney in Chicago.
Support for prompt heating oil was pegged at the psychological level of 70.00 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
